author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Archipelago Anarchist Archive, Perpustakaan Anarkis, and Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (A Brief Introduction)
content:
Initiatives in anarchist archiving, librarianship, and journals of archives & libraries in Indonesia

The Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) is an informal, alternative archives and library initiative established in 2024 with the aim of preserving and distributing anti-authoritarian materials. AAA is driven by a number of anarchist archivists and librarians from various cities in Indonesia.

The materials that AAA focuses on are those produced in, and related to, the archipelago (known as Indonesia), whether in Indonesian or in non-Indonesian languages. These materials can take the form of texts, photographs, audio, video, and so on. All of AAA's digital archive collections can be accessed through the Internet Archive.

Link to the Archipelago Anarchist Archive collection: https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis (Anarchist Library) is an preservation and distribution project for anti-authoritarian materials based on plain text. Plain text was chosen because it makes it easier for authors and translators to distribute their work, easier for publishers to reproduce it, and easier for those who wish to archive it[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis understands anti-authoritarianism in a flexible manner, though not without limits. Therefore, it can be said that Perpustakaan Anarkis accepts and includes both anarchist materials (from all tendencies, except anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism) and materials that can enrich anarchism, such as avant-garde(ism) that challenges not only the boundaries of art but also the state and centralized power, libertarian Marxism, autonomism, democratic confederalism, and so on. In addition, Perpustakaan Anarkis also accepts and includes reportage from the front lines (confrontation) and the home front (care) of flashpoints of popular struggle and resistance, labor strikes, and so on.

Because in anarchism, decentralization and prefiguration are important. And by practicing decentralization and prefiguration, we (and us all) no longer need to wait to act and be overly dependent on a single central point.

Besides anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism, Perpustakaan Anarkis is also not intended for authoritarian Marxists, misanthropic individuals, extractive technologism (automation that subordinates), avant-garde(ism) that leads to fascism, and other authoritarian tendencies and centralized power.

[1] Authors and translators can distribute their works without the hassle of layout, editing, cover design, and other technical work. Conversely, publishers no longer need to go through the trouble of dealing with writing and translation. And archivists—in addition to finding archiving easier—will receive various versions of the work.

Link to the Perpustakaan Anarkis collection: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (Anarsip: Journal of Anti-authoritarian Archives & Libraries) (published periodically, every 6 months) is a space for theorizing–practicing–theorizing–practicing anarchist archives and librarianship. Because we believe that anarchist archives and librarianship should not stop at merely the definition of "managed by, and archiving materials of, anarchist(s) and/or anti-authoritarian [movements and ideas]," but also means using methods, practicing ways of working, and thinking in an anarchist and/or anti-authoritarian manner. If the Situationist International said "to be avant-garde is to move in step with reality" (Internationale Situationiste #8); then we say "to be anarchist archiving and librarianship is to move in step with reality and anarchism."

Link to follow the developments of Anarsip: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/anarsip-jurnal-arsip-perpustakaan-anti-otoritarian

Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) adalah inisiatif pengarsipan dan perpustakaan informal nan alternatif yang didirikan pada tahun 2024 dengan tujuan mempreservasi sekaligus mendistribusi materi-materi anti-otoritarian. AAA digerakkan oleh sejumlah arsiparis dan pustakawan anarkis yang berasal dari berbagai kota di Indonesia.

Adapun materi-materi yang menjadi fokus dari AAA adalah materi-materi yang diproduksi di, dan yang berkaitan dengan, wilayah kepulauan (yang kini disebut sebagai Indonesia) baik itu yang berbahasa Indonesia maupun yang berbahasa non-indonesia. Dan materi-materi tersebut bisa berupa teks, foto, audio, video, dan lain sebagainya. Semua koleksi arsip digital AAA bisa diakses melalui Internet Archive.

Tautan menuju koleksi Archipelago Anarchist Archive: https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis adalah proyek pengarsipan sekaligus pendistribusian materi-materi anti-otoritarian berbasis teks polos (plain text). Teks polos dipilih, karena dapat memudahkan penulis dan penerjemah untuk mendistribusikan karyanya, memudahkan penerbit untuk mereproduksinya, dan memudahkan pihak-pihak yang ingin mengarsipkannya[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis memahami anti-otoritarianisme secara luwes, meski bukan berarti tak terbatas. Karenanya, dapat dikatakan: Perpustakaan Anarkis menerima dan memasukkan baik itu materi-materi anarkisme (dari segala kecenderungan, kecuali anarko-kapitalisme dan anarko-nasionalisme), maupun materi-materi yang dapat memperkaya anarkisme seperti avant-garde(isme) yang tidak hanya menentang batasan seni tetapi juga negara dan kekuasaan tersentral, marxisme-libertarian, otonomisme, konfederalisme demokratis, dan seterusnya. Selain itu, Perpustakaan Anarkis juga menerima dan memasukkan materi-materi reportase dari garis depan (konfrontasi) maupun garis belakang (perawatan) titik-titik api perjuangan dan perlawanan warga, pemogokan buruh, dan lain-lain.

Karena dalam anarkisme, desentralisasi dan prefigurasi itu penting. Dan dengan mempraktikkan desentralisasi dan prefigurasi, kami (dan kita) tidak perlu lagi menunggu untuk bertindak dan terlalu bergantung pada satu titik sentral.

Selain kepada anarko-kapitalisme dan anarko-nasionalisme, Perpustakaan Anarkis juga tidak ditujukan kepada para marxis-otoriter, individu misantropis, teknologiisme yang mengekstraksi (otomatisasi yang mensubordinasi), avant-garde(isme) yang mengarah pada fasisme, dan kecenderungan otoriter serta kekuasaan tersentral lainnya.

[1] Penulis dan penerjemah dapat mendistribusikan karya-karyanya tanpa perlu repot-repot melakukan penataan letak, penyuntingan, merancang sampul, dan kerja-kerja teknis lainnya. Sebaliknya, para penerbit tidak lagi perlu bersusah payah mengurusi penulisan dan penerjemahan karya. Dan para pengarsip—selain menjadi lebih mudah dalam mengarsipkan—akan menerima beragam versi dari karya tersebut.

Tautan menuju koleksi Perpustakaan Anarkis: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (terbit berkala, setiap 6 bulan) adalah wadah untuk menteorisasi-praktik-teorisasi-praktik pengarsipan dan perpustakaan anarkis. Karena kami percaya, pengarsipan dan perpustakaan anarkis tidak boleh berhenti sekadar pada definisi "dikelola oleh, dan mengarsipkan materi, anarkis(me) dan/atau anti-otoritarian", tetapi juga berarti menggunakan metode, mempraktikkan cara kerja, dan berpikir secara anarkis(me) dan/atau anti-otoritarian. Jika Situasionist International mengatakan "untuk menjadi avant-garde berarti bergerak beriringan dengan realitas" (Internationale Situationiste #8); maka kami mengatakan "untuk menjadi pengarsipan dan perpustakaan anarkis berarti bergerak beriringan dengan realitas dan anarkisme".

Tautan untuk mengikuti perkembangan Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/anarsip-jurnal-arsip-perpustakaan-anti-otoritarian

author: Majid00
title: فریدریش انگلس و نقد اقتصاد سیاسی   ِ   مارکس
content: مقالۀ «طرح‌واره‌ای برای نقد اقتصاد سیاسی» به قلم انگلس در سال۱۸۴۳ ، نقطۀ عزیمت اثر سترگی شد که مارکس چهار دهۀ پایانی عمر خویش را صرف نگارش آن کرد. با این حال، انگلس در هیچ‌یک از نوشته‌های متأخر خود، که مدعی بازنمایی و تبیین دیدگاه‌های مارکس بود، نتوانست آن ابعاد بنیادینی از اندیشۀ مارکس را دریابد که خودِ مارکس آن‌ها را حیاتی و اساسی می‌دانست. از آنجا که نوشته¬های انگلس تأثیری ژرف بر قرائت‌های بعدی از کتاب سرمایه بر جای گذاشته‌اند، اذعان به این غفلت و کاستی می‌تواند به ما یاری رساند تا مقصود و غایت واقعی مارکس را در پژوهش‌هایش بازشناسیم.

title: We Need Solidarity Unions - Workers Solidarity Club
content:
Introductory leaflet by the Workers Solidarity Club from Youngstown Ohio, circa early 1980s. List of contacts include Alice and Staughton Lynd.

Ah! That’s quite a nice journey here then :-) Thanks as ever for sharing and for keeping this stuff safe.

Yes thanks to both of you, and Nate!

author: greensyndic
title: Speed Kills: Snuff Capitalist Acceleration - Jeff Shantz
content:
The elimination of jobs at the workplace now coincides with the elimination of former workers outside the workplace under snuff capitalism. And this elimination too must be done in accelerating rates. Time, as always, is money from capital’s perspective. From Anarcho-Syndicalist Review, 95, Fall 2026.

Whether we like it or not, capital is accelerationist. Speed up is built right into the very engine of capitalism. Capital’s drive for accumulation, in competition with other capital for profit, means that it must always go faster, must always accelerate exploitation and value extraction. This is the drive behind the ceaseless, permanent, push for technological advance, from motors to assembly lines to robots to computers, to AI, and beyond.

Speed is the means by which capital beats its competitors in extracting value. More surplus value in an ever-shorter period of time. Any worker knows the tyranny of the clock in the capitalist workplace. Marx suggests that this surplus value extraction is either absolute, the lengthening of the working say, so we work longer beyond the point that we produce the value equivalent to our wages or relative, narrowing the time it takes us to produce the equivalent of our wages. Relative surplus value is the logic of the speed up—using technology to get us producing more and faster. Both forms of extraction, though, dominate the worker’s lifetime.
